episode.title: Restore sessions under the selected workspace runtime’s storage context
episode.before: At parent 9b716cc0e61ffdd4967665d7c0e3c952cf06d7de, both REST and ACP restore paths selected a workspace runtime and constructed a SessionService with that runtime’s sessionRuntimeBaseDir, but the surrounding asynchronous load/resume operation was not executed inside Storage.runWithResolvedRuntimeBaseDir. Consequently, bridge restore work and nested code consulting Storage.getRuntimeBaseDir could observe the process/default runtime root instead of the selected workspace runtime root.
episode.after: At e0b8bea9e0ba369a0661bc51cbbb9a27555aff48, the REST load/resume critical section and the ACP load/resume critical section are invoked through runWithWorkspaceRuntimeStorage using the selected runtime. The ambient resolved storage root therefore remains pinned to sessionRuntimeBaseDir throughout asynchronous restore work. Tests cover both load and resume through REST with a secondary workspace root and through ACP after runtime replacement with a distinct root.
episode.diff: The change wraps the REST archive-coordinated restore callback in runWithWorkspaceRuntimeStorage(runtime, ...), extracts the ACP archive-coordinated restore callback as restoreInRuntime and invokes it through the same helper, broadens that helper’s parameter type to the minimal sessionRuntimeBaseDir-bearing runtime projection, and adds four parameterized regression cases covering REST load/resume and ACP load/resume against non-default selected runtime roots.

evidence_units.claim: Commit e0b8bea9e0ba369a0661bc51cbbb9a27555aff48 has parent 9b716cc0e61ffdd4967665d7c0e3c952cf06d7de, is titled “fix(cli): restore sessions in selected workspace runtime (#9050),” and modifies the REST route, ACP dispatcher, shared runtime-storage helper, and their tests.
evidence_units.source: issue-bundle.json fields resolved_commit, parent_commit, commit_show_stat, and changed_files_name_status; git show --format=fuller --name-status e0b8bea9e0ba369a0661bc51cbbb9a27555aff48

evidence_units.claim: Before the change, the REST restore path entered archiveCoordinator.runSharedMany directly; after the change, that complete asynchronous critical section is passed to runWithWorkspaceRuntimeStorage(runtime, ...).
evidence_units.source: git diff 9b716cc0e61ffdd4967665d7c0e3c952cf06d7de..e0b8bea9e0ba369a0661bc51cbbb9a27555aff48 -- packages/cli/src/serve/routes/session.ts, around commit lines 3949-4246

evidence_units.claim: Inside the newly scoped REST operation, the selected runtime supplies both the SessionService runtimeBaseDir and the bridge used for loadSession or resumeSession, so storage lookup, metadata recovery, and bridge restoration share one selected-runtime context.

The REST regression test stores a session beneath a secondary runtime root, spies on the selected workspace bridge’s loadSession or resumeSession, performs POST /session/:id/load or /resume, and requires both HTTP 200 and Storage.getRuntimeBaseDir() equal to the secondary runtime root during bridge restoration.
evidence_units.source: e0b8bea9e0ba369a0661bc51cbbb9a27555aff48:packages/cli/src/serve/multi-workspace-sessions.test.ts, parameterized test “runs a cold %s inside the selected workspace runtime root” around lines 2191-2245

evidence_units.claim: Before the change, ACP directly awaited archiveCoordinator.runSharedMany; after the change, it defines restoreInRuntime for that critical section and invokes it through runWithWorkspaceRuntimeStorage(sessionRuntime, restoreInRuntime).

The ACP scoped operation resolves persisted session data with a SessionService configured for sessionRuntime.sessionRuntimeBaseDir and then calls loadSession or resumeSession on the same sessionRuntime bridge.

The ACP regression test writes a stored session under a replacement runtime root, activates that replacement runtime, sends session/load or session/resume, and requires the bridge restore callback to observe the replacement root through Storage.getRuntimeBaseDir(), with no JSON-RPC error and exactly one restore call.
evidence_units.source: e0b8bea9e0ba369a0661bc51cbbb9a27555aff48:packages/cli/src/serve/acp-http/workspace-qualified-acp.test.ts, parameterized test “restores session/%s in the selected runtime storage” around lines 803-866

evidence_units.claim: runWithWorkspaceRuntimeStorage delegates to Storage.runWithResolvedRuntimeBaseDir(runtime.sessionRuntimeBaseDir, fn), establishing the ambient storage context for the callback; the commit narrows its required input contract to Pick<WorkspaceRuntime, 'sessionRuntimeBaseDir'>.
evidence_units.source: e0b8bea9e0ba369a0661bc51cbbb9a27555aff48:packages/cli/src/serve/workspace-runtime-storage.ts lines 12-21 and its diff from parent

evidence_units.claim: The added tests explicitly exercise both restore actions, load and resume, on each affected transport and assert the selected runtime root at the bridge boundary where the prior ambient-context mismatch could surface.
The available bundle identifies PR/issue 9050 as the selected-workspace-runtime restore fix, but its body, comments, timeline, reviews, and status checks are unavailable.

candidate_atomics.name: scope-http-session-restore-to-selected-runtime
candidate_atomics.title: Run HTTP session restoration inside the selected runtime’s storage scope
candidate_atomics.description: Bind the full asynchronous HTTP load/resume critical section—not only its SessionService instance—to the selected workspace runtime’s storage root so nested restoration code observes the correct persisted state.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent cold HTTP load and resume operations from reading or continuing session state under a process-default runtime root when a different workspace runtime was selected.
semantic_action.pre_state: A restore request has selected a workspace runtime whose sessionRuntimeBaseDir may differ from the ambient Storage runtime base directory, while the archive-coordinated asynchronous restore operation is still invoked without an ambient runtime binding.
semantic_action.post_state: The archive-coordinated restore, persisted-session resolution, metadata reads, and selected bridge load/resume call execute with the ambient Storage runtime base directory equal to the selected workspace runtime’s sessionRuntimeBaseDir.
semantic_action.validation: For both load and resume, persist the target session under a secondary runtime root, invoke the HTTP restore route for that workspace, assert success, and assert the selected bridge observes that secondary root through Storage.getRuntimeBaseDir().

candidate_atomics.name: scope-acp-session-restore-to-selected-runtime
candidate_atomics.title: Run ACP session restoration inside the selected runtime’s storage scope
candidate_atomics.description: Bind the complete asynchronous ACP load/resume critical section to the selected or replacement workspace runtime so bridge restoration and nested storage access remain aligned with runtime selection.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent ACP load and resume operations from restoring session state under a stale or default storage root after workspace-runtime selection or replacement.
semantic_action.pre_state: An ACP restore request has resolved a sessionRuntime with its own sessionRuntimeBaseDir, but the asynchronous archive-coordinated restore callback is invoked outside that runtime’s ambient Storage context.
semantic_action.post_state: Persisted-session lookup, metadata recovery, and the selected runtime bridge’s load/resume operation execute while Storage resolves paths from sessionRuntime.sessionRuntimeBaseDir.
semantic_action.validation: For both protocol load and resume, activate a replacement runtime with a distinct storage root, store the session there, issue the request, and assert no protocol error, one restore call, and observation of the replacement root inside the bridge callback.

candidate_workflows.name: preserve-selected-runtime-context-across-session-restore
candidate_workflows.title: Preserve workspace runtime context throughout session restoration
candidate_workflows.description: A partial-order resolution workflow for restore paths that select the correct workspace runtime explicitly but lose that selection through an ambient storage API during asynchronous load or resume work.

workflow_graph.goal: Ensure every supported cold session load/resume entry point restores persisted state and invokes its bridge under the storage root owned by the selected workspace runtime.
when_to_use: A service supports multiple workspace runtimes or runtime replacement, with separate persisted-session roots.
The restore path passes an explicit runtime root to one service but nested asynchronous restore code also consults an ambient or context-local storage root.
Restoration succeeds in the primary/default workspace but fails, misses state, or observes the wrong root for a secondary or replacement runtime.
anti_goals: Do not merge or relocate session stores between workspace runtimes.
Do not change session identifiers, restore metadata, archive-lock semantics, bridge ownership, or load/resume response shapes.
Do not replace workspace selection logic; preserve the already selected runtime and propagate its storage context.
Do not globally mutate a process-wide storage root when a callback-scoped binding is available.
not_applicable_when: All session storage access is explicitly parameterized and no restore dependency consults ambient runtime state.
The requested session is absent from the correctly selected runtime store rather than hidden by a context mismatch.
The operation creates a new session and does not restore persisted state.
Only one immutable runtime root exists and runtime selection or replacement cannot occur.
inputs: Restore entry points and their load/resume branches
Ambient storage-context API with asynchronous callback propagation
Tests capable of creating distinct runtime roots
workflow_graph.entry_state: Workspace selection returns the intended runtime, and direct service construction may use its root, but the enclosing asynchronous restoration chain can still observe a different ambient storage root.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Every affected load/resume entry point scopes its complete restore critical section to the selected runtime root, and regression tests prove the selected or replacement root is visible at the bridge boundary for both actions.

steps.condition: The product exposes an HTTP session load/resume route that selects among workspace runtimes.
steps.validation: A session stored only beneath a secondary runtime root can be loaded and resumed through HTTP, and the selected bridge observes that root.

steps.condition: The product also exposes ACP or another protocol restore entry point with an independent dispatch path.
steps.validation: After activating a runtime replacement with a distinct root, both protocol load and resume complete without error and the replacement bridge observes its own root.

validation_ladder: Inspect each restore entry point to confirm runtime selection and ambient storage binding cover the same complete asynchronous critical section.
For the HTTP path, store sessions only under a non-default secondary root and verify both load and resume return success while the bridge observes that root.
For the protocol path, activate a replacement runtime with a distinct root and verify both load and resume use the replacement bridge under that root.
Retain existing restore locking, session-resolution, metadata, isolation, ownership, and response behavior inside the scoped callback.
stop_conditions: Stop if the selected runtime does not expose a stable session storage root.
Stop and diagnose runtime-selection logic if the wrong runtime or bridge is chosen before storage scoping begins.
Stop if correct behavior requires moving or sharing persisted state across runtime boundaries; that is a different migration or ownership problem.
Stop if scoping only a synchronous prefix does not propagate through awaited restore work; the context mechanism must support the complete asynchronous callback.
unresolved_or_deferred: The evidence bundle does not include CI status checks or review discussion.
Tests were inspected as committed regression oracles; no clean test execution result is available from the provided checkout.
ACP is a repository-specific transport instance; applicability to another project requires an equivalent independent restore entry point rather than the same protocol.

unresolved_questions: The GitHub bundle omits the PR body, reviews, comments, timeline, and status checks, so the original reporter’s exact observed failure and CI outcome cannot be established beyond the implementation and committed tests.
The working checkout has widespread pre-existing deletions, so validation is grounded in the pinned commit’s test code rather than a newly executed test run.
